name: Jin Dynasty (266–420)
summary: The Sima family dynasty that briefly reunited China in 280. Civil war and invasions drove it south in 317, where the Eastern Jin ruled from Jiankang while the north split into the Sixteen Kingdoms.

location.value: All of China (Western Jin, 280–316), then south China only (Eastern Jin, 317–420).

terrain.value: The Yellow River plain under the Western Jin, then the Yangtze valley under the Eastern Jin.

climate.value: A colder period that may have pushed steppe peoples south.

resources.value: Farmland of the north, then rice land in the south opened by northern refugees.

disasters.value: Famine and epidemics during the civil wars of the early 4th century.

population.value: No reliable estimate; a census of 280 counted about 16 million people.

disease.value: Epidemics during the wars of the early 4th century.

migration.value: A large migration of northern Han Chinese south of the Yangtze after the sack of Luoyang (311).

economicBase.value: Agriculture on large estates owned by great families.

tradeRoutes.value: River and sea trade in the south; Silk Road links weakened.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: Bronze cash coins and taxes in grain and cloth.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Jin dynasty (266–420) (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lewis, China Between Empires (2009)

inequality.value: Aristocratic clans dominated land and office.

governmentType.value: Monarchy; Eastern Jin emperors were limited by powerful clans.

keyRulers.value: Emperor Wu (Sima Yan, 266–290), Emperor Yuan (318–323), Emperor Gong (last).

succession.value: Hereditary in the Sima family, often controlled by regents.

institutions.value: The nine-rank system favoured aristocrats for government jobs.

stability.value: The War of the Eight Princes (291–306) wrecked the Western Jin.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Jin dynasty (266–420) (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lewis, China Between Empires (2009)

eliteConflict.value: Princes of the Sima family fought each other; later great clans dominated the Eastern Jin.
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Jin dynasty (266–420) (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lewis, China Between Empires (2009)

armyAndTech.value: Heavy cavalry with stirrups appeared in this era.

majorWars.value: War of the Eight Princes; the uprisings of non-Han peoples traditionally called the “Upheaval of the Five Barbarians” (304); Battle of Fei River (383).

territoryChange.value: Reunited China in 280 but lost the north after 316.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Jin dynasty (266–420) (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lewis, China Between Empires (2009)

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: Han-Zhao, Later Zhao, Former Qin and the other Sixteen Kingdoms.

inventions.value: The stirrup appears in China in this era.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Jin dynasty (266–420) (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lewis, China Between Empires (2009)

scienceEducation.value: Ge Hong’s works on alchemy and medicine.

openness.value: Buddhism spread widely, with translators such as Kumarajiva active in the north.

religion.source: Wikipedia: Jin dynasty (266–420) (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lewis, China Between Empires (2009)

languageWriting.value: Chinese; the calligrapher Wang Xizhi lived in this period.

artsArchitecture.value: Wang Xizhi’s calligraphy (Lantingji Xu, 353); Gu Kaizhi’s paintings.

socialStructure.value: Great aristocratic clans, commoners and dependants.

sharedIdentity.value: Han Chinese culture preserved in exile in the south.

neighbours.value: Han-Zhao, Former Qin and other northern states; Goguryeo.

colonisation.value: Northern migrants moved south and developed the Yangtze region.

riseSignals.value: The conquest of Wu (280) briefly reunited China.

peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Jin dynasty (266–420) (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lewis, China Between Empires (2009)

declineSignals.value: Sack of Luoyang (311) and loss of Chang’an (316).

outcome.value: Liu Yu usurped the throne in 420, founding the Liu Song.

sources.value: Book of Jin. Checked against Wikipedia (“Jin dynasty (266–420)”).

overallCertainty.value: Good. Based on the Book of Jin and other official histories.

knownFor.label: Battle of Fei River
knownFor.note: Eastern Jin defeated a much larger Former Qin army.
